Article Title: Amid 'very long meetings' and running chess world, has Viswanathan Anand lost 'hunger' to win? | Exclusive
Article Text:
Viswanathan Anand

Viswanathan Anand at GCL

Generally, I stick to my routine, that's all. It's not like I will keep a lot of FIDE meetings Viswanathan Anand

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The English vocabulary sometimes feels the loss for words while describing what Viswanathan Anand is to India and its chess legacy. There is a particular kind of stillness that follows the Chennai-born Grandmaster into a room, the stillness of a man who solved most of what chess could throw at him decades ago and has nothing left to prove to anyone in it.For over a month now, that stillness has been sitting in a very different chair. On July 24, 2026, Anand became interim President of FIDE, world chess's governing body, after Arkady Dvorkovich voluntarily stepped back from his duties under European Union and Swiss sanctions. The role is temporary by design as Anand's term runs out with the FIDE presidential elections on September 26.But for the two months he holds it, the man who has spent a lifetime being chess's most recognisable player is also, quite literally, running the sport."Fairly, (it's) kind of what I expected," the 56-year-old tells TimesofIndia.com during an exclusive interaction, with that familiar half-smile doing most of the talking before the next sentences catch up."It's more work than being deputy president. When I was the deputy, I only had to step in when Arkady (Dvorkovich) couldn't make it. Now, in fact, I have to conduct a lot of the federation. But I've been doing it out of India mostly."The extra weight of countless responsibilities hasn't meant more miles, though."Actually, I've travelled less, but because I had already made plans like this. I've been attending many, many more meetings, quite often, very long Zoom meetings with lots of people from all over the world to discuss FIDE matters," added the former five-time world champion.The intensity, he says, has already peaked and passed."There was a period last week when that all peaked," he revealed. "Now everything, the agenda, is set for the General Assembly in Samarkand at the end of the year. For the last few days, it's been a bit lighter."And with that, amid the Zoom calls and federation business, the game of 64 squares has called in a more familiar manner.Anand returns to the Global Chess League (GCL) this year with Alaskan Knights. None of that administrative weight, it turns out, has dulled his appetite for the board."I can tell you my hunger for the GCL trophy is still there. I would very much love for us, though I'm playing with Alaskan Knights this year, to pull that off. I'm very motivated, and I hope to do my best and get us into the final first," the Grandmaster, who was one of the most prominent faces of Ganges Grandmasters for the last three seasons, remarked."It doesn't matter what you did in your career. If you're playing this tournament, then you enjoy it, and you try to play. The GCL is not the kind of event, typical event, that I used to play in. It is really a new kind of experience. For those 10 days to two weeks, I really enjoy myself."It may be a new team this year, but the fundamentals have not changed for Anand. "Many players in the GCL have already changed teams a couple of times. I think once I go there and meet my teammates, on the first day itself, it'll feel normal. I have played with Arjun before; two years ago, he was my teammate. There are familiar faces, and you'll just adjust," he remarked.Balancing a federation's crisis, family matters, and then chess, on paper, may look like a nightmare. But ask Anand, and then see the stillness follow."Generally, I stick to my routine, that's all. It's not like I will keep a lot of FIDE meetings; if there's some FIDE emergency, I might take a decision quickly, but otherwise I don't expect to have long meetings while I'm there. I focus very much on the GCL," he told this website, adding that he doesn't plan days in advance so much as meet them as they come."I know that I have to play against somebody tomorrow and I will get ready for it."Within weeks, the presidency will pass to someone else. Until then, world chess is being run by a man who, when the meetings end, still just wants to play. And according to Anand, the play, on offer between September 5-13 in Bengaluru, will be as competitive as "anywhere else".ALSO READ: 'Praggnanandhaa is No. 1 in the world': Viswanathan Anand after India's first Grand Chess Tour title "Of course, they are (competitive). Because of the kind of openings they play, you could think, 'Oh, they're not taking it seriously.' But in fact, they're simply adapting their approach for the faster time control, for the pressure of watching your teammates and making decisions based on the match situation," he concluded. "Once you take into account the different atmosphere, they are just as competitive as they are anywhere else. "
Article Summary: Viswanathan Anand is interim President of FIDE, world chess's governing body. Anand's term runs out with the FIDE presidential elections on September 26. The 56-year-old returns to the Global Chess League (GCL) this year with Alaskan Knights.

Article Title: Pakistan cricket in turmoil: PCB selector demands inquiry into Imam-ul-Haq injury after opener didn't bat at Lord's
Article Text:
Imam-ul-Haq

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A senior member of Pakistan's selection committee has questioned the seriousness of Imam-ul-Haq's calf injury and called for an inquiry after the opener did not bat in either innings during Pakistan's 194-run defeat to England in the second Test at Lord's.Aaqib Javed, who is part of Pakistan's four-member selection panel, said the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) will investigate how Imam was managed after suffering the injury during the match."An inquiry will be conducted into this matter," Aaqib Javed told Pakistan's private news channel Geo TV during an interview aired on Tuesday night, as quoted by news agency AP.Javed questioned how a player could miss both innings because of a muscle injury."How is it possible that you failed to come out to bat in both innings after pulling up a muscle?" Javed said.He added that players have batted through injuries in the past and described Imam's case as a matter of concern."Injuries do occur and we have seen instances in the past where players -- even with casts -- have gone out and made an effort. This situation is different. It is a matter of great concern, and action will be taken regarding it."Imam injured his calf while fielding on the opening day of the Lord's Test and took no further part in the match.After former chief selector Mohammad Wasim questioned Imam's absence, the opener appeared on the outfield before play on the fourth day. He was seen shadow batting with his left calf heavily strapped but was visibly limping.Imam was one of seven players recalled from England after Pakistan lost the first two Tests at Headingley and Lord's. Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul were also sent back by the PCB.Pakistan have appointed white-ball head coach Mike Hesson and bowling coach Ashley Noffke to take charge of the team for the third Test, which starts in Birmingham on September 9.The selectors have picked five uncapped players for the final Test, along with openers Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal, who have played a combined 10 Tests.Javed also addressed reports of differences between the selectors and the team management over the playing XI for the Lord's Test.According to Javed, he wanted the team to include fast-bowling all-rounder Ubaid Shah, wicketkeeper-batter Ghazi Ghori and another pace option instead of Mohammad Rizwan. Instead, only Salman Ali Agha was dropped after leading Pakistan in the first Test in Babar Azam's absence."We can't just keep waiting,” Javed said. “I had actually spoken to both the captain and the coach after the first Test, suggesting they include Ubaid, who bowls at 140 kph. Agha was rightly rested, Ghazi Ghori was available on the tour and should have played instead of Rizwan."
Article Summary: Aaqib Javed questions the seriousness of Imam-ul-Haq's calf injury. The opener did not bat in either innings during Pakistan's defeat to England. Pakistan Cricket Board will investigate how Imam was managed. Javed also addressed reports of differences between the selectors and team management.

Article Title: In 2014, India made mid-tour coaching shake-up during England tour, brought in Ravi Shastri and new assistant coaches; how did MS Dhoni's team perform then? Revisiting as Pakistan tear up Test squad,
Article Text:
Sarfaraz Ahmed, Babar Azam (left), and MS Dhoni, Ravi Shastri

When India changed coaches during the England tour in 2014

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Pakistan pushed the panic button and made major changes to their Test setup after losing the first two Tests against England, dropping seven players and replacing two members of the coaching staff ahead of the third and final Test in Birmingham.After a 194-run defeat at Lord's, which gave England an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series, the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) decided to overhaul both the squad and the support staff.Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul have been called back to Pakistan. They will be replaced by white-ball head coach Mike Hesson and bowling coach Ashley Noffke for the final Test starting on September 9.The PCB has also sent home seven players. Wicketkeeper Mohammad Rizwan, opener Imam-ul-Haq, Salman Ali Agha, spinner Ali Usman and fast bowler Khurram Shahzad, many of whom featured in the Lord's Test, have been dropped from the squad. All-rounder Aamir Jamal and batter Awais Zafar have also returned home without playing a match on the tour.Sarfaraz's three-month spell as head coach ended after Pakistan lost five of their six away Tests under him — two against Bangladesh, one against the West Indies and two against England.Babar Azam's return as Test captain has also failed to improve Pakistan's results. He replaced Shan Masood as captain in May and drew the West Indies series 1-1 before Pakistan lost the first two Tests in England.Pakistan have now lost 10 of their last 11 away Test matches.India made similar changes during their tour of England in 2014 after a poor Test series.India won the second Test at Lord’s to go 1-0 up in the five-match series before losing the next three heavily, including a humiliating innings and 244-run defeat within three days at The Oval in the final outing.After the series defeat, the BCCI reshuffled the support staff for the ODI series against England.Former India captain Ravi Shastri was appointed Director of Cricket, while Duncan Fletcher continued as head coach.The BCCI also gave bowling coach Joe Dawes and fielding coach Trevor Penney a "break" for the ODI series. Sanjay Bangar and former India fast bowler Bharat Arun joined as assistant coaches, while R. Sridhar became the fielding coach.The BCCI had said: "In their continuing efforts to re-energise the support to the team, the BCCI has given a break to the bowling coach Mr Joe Dawes and the fielding coach, Mr Trevor Penny for the one day series and appointed Mr Sanjay Bangar, former Indian all rounder and former India fast bowler Mr Bharat Arun as the Asst. coaches of the team. Mr R.Sridhar will join the support team as the fielding coach for the one day series. "India went on to win the five-match ODI series 3-1. After first ODI was washed out in Bristol, India went on to win the next three games in Cardiff, Nottingham, and Bermingham, respectively, before losing the last ODI in Leeds.
Article Summary: Sarfaraz Ahmed and Umar Gul have been called back to Pakistan. They will be replaced by white-ball head coach Mike Hesson and bowling coach Ashley Noffke. The PCB has also sent home seven players. India made similar changes during their tour of England in 2014 after a poor Test series.

Article Title: 'The more you bowl, the stronger you become': Gurnoor Brar
Article Text:
Gurnoor Brar

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bengaluru: In a crowded Indian pace pool, opportunities have to be seized. Punjab's Gurnoor Brar appears to have taken that lesson to heart. The lanky pacer made an immediate impression on his India ODI debut against Afghanistan in June, claiming three wickets. A month later, representing India 'A', he followed it up with a 10-wicket match haul against Sri Lanka 'A' in Galle.Brar's schedule has been relentless. He flew in from Sri Lanka on Friday and turned up for the Duleep Trophy semifinal against South Zone at the BCCI Centre of Excellence on Sunday. Despite bowling 23 overs on a slow-paced surface, he maintained his intensity and finished with a four-wicket match haul in the first innings.For now, though, workload is not something that worries the 25-year-old. He believes the demands of fast bowling are best embraced rather than feared. "I have always believed in training my body to high loads. No matter how much I bowl, it should not matter. I enjoy bowling more. Breaks are needed, obviously, but it is all planning. And the more we push our bodies, the stronger they get. I have an old fast bowler's mindset: the more you bowl, the stronger you become.Brar's rise has been built on sustained performances. He took 30 wickets from nine matches in the last two Ranji Trophy seasons, earned his maiden Test call-up for the one-off Afghanistan Test and was subsequently picked for the Sri Lanka tour. The speedster is yet to make his Test debut but the last three months have offered an invaluable lesson alongside Jasprit Bumrah , Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna and other seniors."I was performing well in the Ranji Trophy; I also did well for India 'A' and I was picked on that basis. But I've learned how to stay consistent with my lengths and bowl on different wickets. I've been growing well under Morne sir (bowling coach Morkel), Gambhir sir (head coach), 'Boom' (Jasprit Bumrah), Siraj and Prasidh. Seeing them prepare, I have developed," said Brar, who has taken 11 wickets in six ODIs.The biggest lesson from the senior pros, he said, was not to abandon what brought him this far. "The learnings from Bumrah and other seniors were to stick to my strengths and not change. But the important thing is to understand bowling in different conditions. Things come along with the experience of playing more matches," he said.
Article Summary: Punjab's Gurnoor Brar made his India ODI debut against Afghanistan in June. He followed it up with a 10-wicket match haul against Sri Lanka 'A' in Galle. Brar flew in from Sri Lanka on Friday and turned up for the Duleep Trophy semifinal on Sunday.

Article Title: Sourav Ganguly to attend BCCI AGM on September 18 in Mumbai
Article Text:
Sourav Ganguly

MUMBAI: Former India captain Sourav Ganguly will attend the BCCI Annual General Meeting on September 18 at the BCCI HQ here, as the representative of the Bengal Cricket Association, of which he is the president.31 out of 35 state units will attend the BCCI AGM, with four state associations being left unrepresented due to various issues.The cricket associations of Hyderabad, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh and Bihar will not be represented at the BCCI AGM, while the Maharashtra Cricket Association will be represented by Court-appointed administrator Govinda Sanap. Former India seamer Venkatesh Prasad will represent the Karnataka State Cricket Association, while ex-India batter Saurabh Tiwary will represent the Jharkhand State Cricket Association.The Mumbai Cricket Association will be represented in the AGM by Unmesh Khanvilkar.

Article Title: Carlos Alcaraz makes winning US Open return after wrist injury: ‘I had more nerves than usual’
Article Text:
Carlos Alcaraz, of Spain, celebrates winning a match against Roman Safiullin, of Russia, during the first round of the U.S. Open tennis championships, Monday, Aug. 31, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo/Sydney Schaefer)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Sabalenka starts title defence

Carlos Alcaraz made a winning return to Grand Slam tennis at the US Open on Monday, and the biggest positive was that his injured right wrist felt completely fine.The 23-year-old Spaniard beat Roman Safiullin 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 despite missing the French Open and Wimbledon since April.“I don’t know how it looked from outside, but from inside, my feeling was that I was hitting normal,” Alcaraz said. “I was playing pretty normal, playing my style, and yeah, the arm, the wrist, everything felt great.”Alcaraz admitted he was more nervous than usual because he had not played a Grand Slam match for several months. Still, he said his main aim was to enjoy the tournament and see how his body responds.“I had more nerves than usual, but just happy, because, for me, my goal here is to compete, to enjoy, and let’s see how my body’s going to react after the matches, after the competition again,” Alcaraz said.“I don’t know how far I’m going to go in the tournament. I didn’t know if I was going to lose this one, if I’m going to make the second round, final. I don’t know how far I’m going to go. But what I just really want to do is enjoy every time that I’m going to walk into the court feeling the energy from the people, feel the competition.”His chances of defending the title have received a boost after Novak Djokovic suffered a shock first-round defeat, while top-ranked Jannik Sinner is sidelined with a knee injury.Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka also began strongly, beating Camila Osorio 6-4, 6-4. She is aiming to become the first player since Serena Williams to win three straight US Open titles.“I feel like this is one of my favorite stadiums,” Sabalenka told the crowd afterward. “I really experienced the best emotions here in this stadium.”Meanwhile, Stefanos Tsitsipas eliminated 10th seed Arthur Fils and was asked whether he could rediscover his best form.“Why not?” Tsitsipas said.
Article Summary: Carlos Alcaraz makes winning return to Grand Slam tennis at US Open. Spaniard beat Roman Safiullin despite missing French Open and Wimbledon. Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka also began strongly. Stefanos Tsitsipas eliminated 10th seed Arthur Fils.

Article Title: Rohit Rajpal throws hat into ring for AITA president’s post
Article Text:
DLTA president Rohit Rajpal announces candidature for All India Tennis Association presidency

New Delhi:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Rohit Rajpal has thrown his hat into the ring for the All India Tennis Association (AITA) president’s post, setting up a potentially keen contest ahead of elections likely to be held in late Oct or early Nov this year.The AITA is currently functioning under the interim supervision of court-appointed administrator, retired Justice Gita Mittal. The administrator has opened the process for Sportsperson of Outstanding Merit (SOM) candidates seeking to contest the elections for AITA office-bearer posts.Rajpal, 55, will contest through the general body and file his nomination through his state association. He is currently president of the Delhi Lawn Tennis Association (DLTA), an Executive Committee member of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA), an AITA office-bearer and the non-playing captain of the Indian Davis Cup team.“It is after a lot of introspection and interactions with well-wishers in the tennis fraternity and other friends that I have decided to contest the forthcoming elections of the prestigious All India Tennis Association as President,” Rajpal said in a statement.“Tennis is not just a sport for me; it has been my life since the time I was a young boy who wished to make it big. At 55, when many summers have passed, my heart still beats for Indian tennis.It is my dream and vision for India that a sport which has produced so many champions at home should grow further by leaps and bounds,” he added.Rajpal, a former Asian Junior champion and Asian Games medallist whose playing career was cut short by a serious back injury, said his experience in tennis administration and the Davis Cup had strengthened his resolve to seek the top post.“Having been involved in tennis matters at large for almost a decade in AITA and DLTA has been a learning and enriching hands-on experience,” he said. “As the non-playing Davis Cup captain of Team India in several Davis Cup engagements, it was enormously satisfying to be with and motivate our immensely talented players to give their best and bring glory to the nation by advancing to the second-round qualifiers.”India will face South Korea in Seoul on September 18-19 for a place in the final eight of the Davis Cup. Rajpal, however, will have to relinquish the Davis Cup captaincy if he is elected AITA president.“This journey has given me the confidence to now step forward and announce my candidature as President of All India Tennis Association as a step forward in my desire to contribute to the growth and development of tennis in India,” Rajpal said.“With your support, I plan to adopt player-centric approach and policies, good governance and transparency above all. I plan to share my vision document in due course,” he added.Chintan Parikh of the Gujarat association is also expected to contest the president’s post. It is learnt that Indian tennis legend and Bengal Tennis Association president Leander Paes could also enter the fray. Paes, who took charge of the Bengal association in Nov 2025, would likely come through the SOM route and file his nomination.
Article Summary: Rohit Rajpal has thrown his hat into the ring for the All India Tennis Association (AITA) president’s post. Rajpal, 55, will contest through the general body and file his nomination through his state association. Bengal Tennis Association president Leander Paes could also enter the fray.

Article Title: Siddhesh Lad to replace Shardul Thakur as Mumbai captain for 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season
Article Text:
Siddhesh Lad and Shardul Thakur (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Mumbai: Mumbai will have a new captain for the second successive Ranji Trophy season, with seasoned batter Siddhesh Lad set to take charge of the 42-time champions in the 2026-27 campaign. Lad will replace allrounder Shardul Thakur , who led Mumbai across formats during the previous domestic season.Confirming the development, Mumbai senior selection committee chairman Rajesh Pawar said the decision was taken keeping both leadership continuity and workload management in mind.“Yes, we’ve decided to appoint Siddhesh as our captain for the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season. He did well last season and is experienced. Shardul is our match-winner. There is already too much workload on him as he’s expected to bowl a lot of overs, take wickets and contribute with the bat as well. We don’t want to burden him with the responsibility of captaincy. Plus, we’ll have to manage his workload. There are 10 games in the Ranji Trophy and he may have to rest for the odd match,” Pawar told TOI on Monday.Pawar said both players had been consulted before the move was finalised.“We’ve spoken to both Siddhesh and Shardul about it, and both are positive about it. Since the season starts with four Ranji Trophy matches in October, we wanted clarity on the captaincy well in advance,” he added.The appointment rewards a stellar domestic season from Lad, who was Mumbai’s standout performer with the bat in the 2025-26 Ranji Trophy. The 34-year-old amassed 774 runs in eight matches at an impressive average of 77.40, striking five centuries to finish as the team’s leading run-scorer.Over the course of an accomplished first-class career, Lad has compiled 5,623 runs in 82 matches at 44.27, including 15 hundreds and 30 fifties. Mumbai begin their Ranji Trophy season against Chandigarh at Wankhede Stadium from Oct 11-14. They are placed in Elite Group D alongside Chandigarh, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Railways, Tamil Nadu and Uttarakhand. Mumbai last lifted the Ranji Trophy in 2023-2024 under Ajinkya Rahane.
Article Summary: Siddhesh Lad will captain Mumbai in the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season. The 34-year-old replaces Shardul Thakur, who led Mumbai across formats last season. Mumbai begin their campaign against Chandigarh at Wankhede Stadium from Oct 11-14.

Article Title: ‘Nothing went according to my plans’: K Humpy opens up ahead of Olympiad title defence
Article Text:
K Humpy

TOI

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

K Humpy, India’s top-ranked woman chess player, was unwilling to state her preferred board number for Team India at the Olympiad. Nor did she say that she would play according to the wishes of the team or captain. But she dropped enough hints.“I have played a few Olympiads and have always played on board one. For many years, we have been following the rating procedure for maintaining the board order. I don’t know how they are going to look at it this year,” Humpy toldfrom Vijayawada on Monday. Top seeds India are set to defend their gold medal in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, starting Sept 16.Humpy finished eighth with 3.5 points in the nine-round classical Cairns Cup in St Louis, USA. But her Norway Chess campaign in May-June, where she finished sixth and last, was particularly disappointing. “It’s not so comfortable to enter into the Olympiad in such a scenario,” said Humpy. “I'm just waiting to get back in good shape. I was a bit rusty but it happens to every player. You’ll be in that bad phase and then you’ll come out of it.On her poor run in Norway, Humpy said, “I played the tournament after a very long gap.Nothing went according to my plans. This year was disturbing. I was also a bit upset with the off-the-board things and probably that also reflected in the way I played.”Humpy withdrew from the Candidates tournament in Cyprus after FIDE turned down her request to shift the eight-player women’s world championship qualifier to a safer venue, citing security concerns arising from the war in West Asia.“I think I’m fine now,” she said. “Probably, it did disturb me for a few months. Like, it’s not easy for a player who has been professional and working towards it and then taking all the negativity. So it did affect me. I spent many sleepless nights as well. But for the last month or so, I have been in better shape.”
Article Summary: K Humpy, India’s top-ranked woman chess player, was unwilling to state her preferred board number for Team India at the Olympiad. Top seeds India are set to defend their gold medal in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, starting Sept 16.

Article Title: ‘Pakistan cricket has hit a panic button’: Ramiz Raja slams PCB over unprecedented England tour overhaul
Article Text:
Pakistan cricket team (ANI Photo)

Ramiz questions unprecedented overhaul

Changes come amid Lord’s controversy

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Pakistan batter and PCB chairman Ramiz Raja has criticised the current board for what he described as a panic-driven response to the team’s disastrous Test tour of England.The PCB made sweeping changes after Pakistan lost the first two Tests of the three-match series, sending seven players home before the final match in Birmingham. Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq and Salman Ali Agha are among those dropped from the tour, while seven replacements have been brought into the squad.The changes have also extended to the coaching staff. Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and assistant coach Umar Gul have been released from their positions, with white-ball coach Mike Hesson set to take charge for the third Test.Ramiz believes the scale and timing of the overhaul could further damage the confidence of the Pakistan players rather than solve the team’s problems.“I'm trying to convince myself this is all OK, but it is not. It just shows Pakistan cricket has hit a panic button. It's not good for the game, it's not good for the confidence of the players who have come in, or for the players who are left, because it makes you a selfish team,” Ramiz, BBC Radio 5 Live.“What is the guarantee they will get the results? Some of these guys have not played Test cricket. I've got no idea why this was done,” he added.Pakistan’s performances in England have been poor from the outset.They suffered an innings defeat in the opening Test at Headingley before England won the Lord’s Test by 194 runs. Across their four innings in the series, Pakistan have failed to reach 200 on every occasion.However, Ramiz questioned whether replacing such a large number of players midway through a tour could suddenly change the team’s fortunes.“I'm really not happy with the situation. How many times have we seen this happen in world cricket? Never, ever. This is more like football, midway through the season, firing a manager. If you ask me how things can be fixed, I've got no idea,” said Ramiz.The former PCB chairman also pointed to the uncertainty created for both the players being sent home and those suddenly brought into the squad.With the third Test fast approaching, several newcomers will be expected to adapt quickly to Test cricket and the conditions in England.The PCB’s drastic decisions have come during an already turbulent tour.The Lord’s Test was played against the backdrop of an off-field dispute involving the sons of former Pakistan captain and prime minister Imran Khan.Sky Sports broadcast an interview with Suleiman and Kasim Khan during the lunch interval on the opening day. The programme focused on their father’s circumstances and prompted reports that the PCB had considered withdrawing Pakistan from the remainder of the Test and potentially the tour.Pakistan ultimately continued playing, while captain Babar Azam and head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed said they were unaware of any plan to boycott the match.The timing of the latest changes has also attracted attention because the Pakistan squad is scheduled to meet King Charles at Clarence House during its stay in the UK.Pakistan will now attempt to salvage something from the tour when they face England in the third and final Test in Birmingham.
Article Summary: Ramiz questions unprecedented overhaul of Pakistan's cricket team. Seven players have been sent home and seven replacements brought in. Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and assistant coach Umar Gul have been released from their positions, with white-ball coach Mike Hesson set to take charge for the third Test.

Article Title: Mahela Jayawardene likely to continue as Mumbai Indians coach; status quo on trade chatter
Article Text:
Mahela Jayawardene (left) and Hardik Pandya

Don't be surprised if he [Hardik Pandya] is not traded at all. Discussions have also happened with the player along these lines. For a trade to happen, multiple things need to fall into place. So it's not that straightforward. Sources

Hardik Pandya

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Former Sri Lanka captain Mahela Jayawardene is likely to continue as Mumbai Indians (MI) head coach for the 2027 edition of the Indian Premier League (IPL), with the franchise reluctant to make sweeping changes. It is learnt that Jayawardene joined the five-time champions on a "two + one" contract in 2024 and could well be given another year, considering it will be the last year of the ongoing cycle. A formal announcement is expected next month, provided there is no late change of heart.Under Jayawardene, Mumbai Indians reached the playoffs in 2025 but finished ninth the following year. 2026 was a disappointing season for the IPL giants, as they won only four games in a campaign marred by injuries, availability concerns and unrest in the dressing room.Since the disappointing last season, there has been a lot of chatter around their captain Hardik Pandya's potential trade. While multiple franchises have expressed interest, there has yet to be any substantial movement on that front.TimesofIndia.com has also learnt that some dialogue has taken place with the Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR), but the lack of a tradeable asset has not excited MI at the moment. Cameron Green's name was on the table, but the MI think tank is wary of the Australian's workload next year, which includes Australia's packed Test calendar.As far as the Chennai Super Kings (CSK) are concerned, some action is expected once they finalise their new head coach.How will MI tackle the Pandya situation? They are keen on retaining him as a player for the upcoming season as they plan to head in a new direction under a new captain. The management has already explored this idea, and it is learnt that former India and MI captain Rohit Sharma is actively involved in discussions about the captaincy and the team's direction. Returning Rohit to the captaincy was also an option, but a new face is likely as the 39-year-old is not keen to wear the armband again. Tilak Varma and Jasprit Bumrah are two potential options, with the scales tilting in the former's favour."Don't be surprised if he is not traded at all. Discussions have also happened with the player along these lines. For a trade to happen, multiple things need to fall into place. So it's not that straightforward," says a source tracking developments.It will be interesting to see how the dynamics unfold if Pandya is not traded at all and how the franchise addresses the dressing room unrest. A change in captaincy is something they expect will restore normalcy, but navigating the turbulence will require significant effort. Another matter that will need attention is that of recently sacked India T20I captain Suryakumar Yadav . Apart from Pandya, there was chatter around the T20 specialist, but the franchise seems in no mood to let go of their experienced campaigner."Yes, he didn't have a good season last year, but what about the ones before that? MI will not discard a player based on one season, and that's not how they operate. They take pride in the 'One Family' tag and swear by it," adds the source.As things stand, continuity has been the bottom line. While a reset cannot be ruled out from the next cycle, there is no desperation for the 2027 edition. A captaincy change is inevitable, but it may not be a surprise if the status quo continues on other matters.
Article Summary: Mahela Jayawardene is likely to continue as Mumbai Indians head coach for the 2027 edition of the Indian Premier League (IPL) The franchise are reluctant to make sweeping changes. A formal announcement is expected next month, provided there is no late change of heart. There has been a lot of chatter around Hardik Pandya's potential trade.

Article Title: 'Good for nothing': Danish Kaneria lambasts Pakistan cricket, calls it 'a shame after 70 years'
Article Text:
Players greet each other at the end of the play on day four of the second cricket test match between England and Pakistan in London, Sunday, Aug. 30, 2026. (AP Photo/Dave Shopland)

Kaneria questions Pakistan’s team and bowling attack

Call for major changes in domestic cricket

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Pakistan spinner Danish Kaneria has strongly criticised the country’s cricket system after Pakistan suffered a 0-2 Test series defeat against England. He questioned the team’s selection, coaching, domestic cricket structure and the lack of accountability within the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB).Pakistan’s 194-run loss at Lord’s gave England an unassailable lead in the series. In response, Pakistan released seven players from the squad and removed head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul. But Kaneria believes changing personnel will not solve the deeper problems.Kaneria said Pakistan’s cricket has lost its competitiveness and the fighting spirit that was once associated with the team. He also criticised the repeated changes in leadership and selection.“It's a shame that after 70 years, Pakistan has gone through such a disaster. There is no logic, selection committee, or play. They are just good for nothing. You see, such a bad performance. If a person loses, he tries and fights before losing. The fight has to be visible. Here, there’s no fight. No one knows anything,” he told news agency IANS.He also questioned why coaches and selectors are appointed for short periods before being removed, saying the system needs stability and people who are willing to take responsibility for both wins and losses.Kaneria was particularly unhappy with Pakistan’s bowling options. He pointed out that experienced players such as Mohammad Abbas, who took nine wickets at Lord’s, and spinner Noman Ali have been overlooked despite performing well.“And the bowling attack is pathetic. Who is Muhammad Shahzad? Where did he come from? He doesn’t have any line or length. No swing, no reverse swing. Nothing.”He also criticised Pakistan’s batting approach in English conditions, particularly the dismissals of Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan.“Like a player of the calibre of Babar Azam is getting out like this. This is pathetic. And then you are keeping Rizwan for so long. I don't know what he is doing. Why is he even there?”Kaneria believes the problems begin well before players reach the national team. He blamed the weakening of domestic cricket and the closure of departmental cricket for reducing the quality of Pakistan’s talent pool.“I like how the BCCI have put in their contracts that first class cricket is important. At least you play 5 to 6 games. None of our boys play domestic. And this downfall of Pakistan cricket started when the structure of domestic cricket changed.”He argued that selectors need to regularly watch domestic matches instead of relying heavily on performances in the Pakistan Super League.“The reason is that the talent pool has been eliminated. There is no doubt there’s talent pool in Pakistan but this selection happens mostly based on PSL.”Kaneria called for a strong selection committee, an experienced coach and a settled group of players who are given enough time to develop.“There are only a few players around whom Pakistan cricket revolves. There is no improvement. Need a strong coach and a strong selection committee.”Above all, he wants Pakistan to regain its competitive spirit.“We also used to lose. But fight and lose. At least fight. Fight, try at least! But there is no effort.”
Article Summary: Former Pakistan spinner Danish Kaneria has strongly criticised the country’s cricket system after Pakistan suffered a 0-2 Test series defeat against England. He questioned the team’S selection, coaching, domestic cricket structure and the lack of accountability within the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB)

Article Title: Big Blow for South Africa! Kagiso Rabada likely to miss Australia Test series with Hamstring Injury
Article Text:
Kagiso Rabada likely to miss Australia Tests (Image: Agency)

Donald confirms Rabada absence

Proteas face pace-bowling concerns

South Africa are likely to suffer a major blow ahead of their three-match Test series against Australia, with premier fast bowler Kagiso Rabada ruled out after sustaining a severe Grade 3 tear in his right hamstring.The injury, picked up during Rabada’s winter conditioning programme, is expected to keep him out for up to 10 weeks, ruling him out of the high-profile series that begins in Durban on October 9.Former South Africa fast bowler and current Lions bowling coach Allan Donald confirmed that Rabada will miss the entire series, ending hopes of having him available for the domestic season.“He’s going to be out for all the Aussie Tests as well,” Donald was quoted as saying by South African media outlet News24 on Sunday.South Africa are scheduled to face Australia in three Tests, with the second match in Gqeberha from October 18 and the final Test in Cape Town from October 27. The series will be preceded by a three-match ODI series beginning in Durban on September 24.Rabada’s absence leaves a significant void in the South African bowling attack. Gerald Coetzee Corbin Bosch and youngster Kwena Maphaka are likely to shoulder greater responsibility in his absence. South Africa are also monitoring the fitness of Nandre Burger, who is recovering from a stress fracture in his back.However, there is still a chance that the left-arm pacer could recover in time to feature in the Test series.Meanwhile, Rabada has taken 340 wickets in 73 Tests and played a key role in South Africa’s victory over Australia in the 2025 World Test Championship final at Lord’s, where he finished with match figures of 9-110. He also boasts an impressive record against Australia, having claimed 58 wickets in 11 Tests at an average of 21.39.
Article Summary: Kagiso Rabada ruled out for up to 10 weeks with hamstring injury. South Africa face Australia in three-match Test series starting in Durban on October 9. Rabada has taken 340 wickets in 73 Tests and played a key role in South Africa's victory over Australia in the 2025 World Test Championship final at Lord's.

Article Title: Blow to Stephen Fleming: CSK legend rejects England Test batting coach job ahead of 2027 Ashes
Article Text:
Michael Hussey, left, with MS Dhoni, during the Chennai Super Kings ROAR 2026, pre-season fan event, at M. A. Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai. (PTI File Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Australia batter Michael Hussey has turned down the opportunity to become England’s Test batting coach and is instead set to join Cricket Australia in a part-time consultancy role. The decision comes as a boost for Australia ahead of next year’s Ashes and leaves England Test head coach Stephen Fleming searching for another batting coach.According to a report in The Guardian, Hussey preferred the Australia role because its flexible nature will allow him to continue his existing commitments in franchise cricket, The Hundred and commentary. The 51-year-old had spoken to Fleming last month about joining England’s coaching staff but has decided to remain in Australia.The report said the flexibility offered by Cricket Australia was a key factor in Hussey’s decision, compared with the more demanding role proposed by England and Fleming.Hussey was Welsh Fire’s head coach in The Hundred this year and has also worked as a batting coach for Chennai Super Kings in the Indian Premier League.Fleming and Hussey worked together for 18 years at CSK, first as player and coach, before their association ended this year. Fleming was unable to convince his former colleague to join him with England.Hussey had previously worked with England as a part-time consultant during their successful T20 World Cup campaign in 2022.However, taking up a full-time role as Test batting coach would have involved a heavier workload, with England scheduled to tour South Africa, Bangladesh and Australia this winter before hosting the Ashes next summer.Australia’s Test schedule is also demanding, but Hussey will be able to work around his other commitments under the part-time arrangement.Fleming can continue looking for a batting coach, although the England and Wales Cricket Board could decide to retain Marcus Trescothick. Trescothick has been working as caretaker batting coach during the ongoing Test series against Pakistan.Hussey made his Test debut for Australia as a 30-year-old in late 2005 and went on to play 79 Tests, 185 ODIs and 38 T20Is.He retired from international cricket in January 2013, ending his Test career with 6,235 runs at an average of 51.52. He was also part of Australia’s 2007 World Cup-winning team.
Article Summary: Former Australia batter Michael Hussey has turned down the opportunity to become England’s Test batting coach. Hussey is instead set to join Cricket Australia in a part-time consultancy role. The decision comes as a boost for Australia ahead of next year's Ashes. England Test head coach Stephen Fleming is still searching for a new coach.

4th T20I: October 30, Auckland

New Zealand will host India A for three four-day matches in Christchurch from October 24, giving the players valuable preparation ahead of the senior teams’ two-Test series later in the year.New Zealand Cricket (NZC) confirmed the fixtures while announcing the schedule for the country’s domestic Plunket Shield competition. The three matches will be played alongside India’s white-ball tour of New Zealand.India are set to tour New Zealand from October to December for a busy multi-format assignment featuring five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests. The India A matches will give players an opportunity to adapt to New Zealand conditions before the Test series."The domestic red ball summer will also get an injection of international class as New Zealand A host India A for three four-day matches in Christchurch starting October 24," NZC said in a statement.The exact dates of the three India A matches have not yet been announced, but all three fixtures will be held in Christchurch. India will play Test cricket in New Zealand for the first time since 2019, while their last white-ball assignment in the country came in 2022.New Zealand Cricket also confirmed that its domestic first-class season will run from November 19 to March 29, with a break during the Super Smash and Ford Trophy competitions.

Article Title: Sanju Samson, Jasprit Bumrah return for Afghanistan T20I series; Hardik Pandya unfit

Sanju Samson

Squad

MUMBAI: Hardik Pandya's comeback to India T20I side has been delayed again, with the star all-rounder yet to regain full fitness. However, Sanju Samson , pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah and mystery spinner Varun Chakravarthy have returned as India named a near-full-strength squad for the three-match T20I series against Afghanistan in Delhi from Sept 13-17.Bumrah, who last played a T20I in India's T20 World Cup final win over New Zealand on March 8, has been included subject to fitness after a recurrence of a left knee injury forced him to miss the final ODI in England at Lord's and the subsequent Test series in Sri Lanka. Varun, too, has returned after recovering from a hamstring injury sustained on England tour."Four cricketers have been picked subject to fitne-ss. Article Title: Duleep Trophy: East Zone in final with dominant victory over Central
Article Text:
East Zone's Vaibhav Sooryavanshi plays a shot on day three of the Duleep Trophy Semi-final 1 cricket match between Central Zone and East Zone, at BCCI Centre of Excellence (CoE) grounds, in Bengaluru, Karnataka. (PTI Photo)

North zone fightback

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Brief scores:

North Zone 195 & 256/7 in 66 overs (Sanat Sangwan 76, Ayush Doseja 52, Anshul Kamboj 29 batting; MD Nidheesh 2-47, Kavuri Saiteja 2-34, Shreyas Gopal 2-77) vs. South 312 (o/n: 285/9) in 100.3 overs (Tilak Varma 116 n.o; Arshdeep Singh 2-59, Anshul 2-58, Gurnoor Brar 4-88).

Central 266 & 158 (o/n: 45/3) in 50.2 overs (Aman Mokhade 41; Mukesh Kumar 4-44, Mohammed Shami 3-56) lost to East 266 & 162/6 in 39.3 overs (Vaibhav Sooryavanshi 40, Ishan Kishan 39; Harsh Dubey 4-53).

BENGALURU: On a day when 13 wickets fell, East Zone had the final say in the Duleep Trophy semifinal at the BCCI CoE here. The Ishan Kishan-led side dominated proceedings in the second innings to claim a four-wicket victory over Central Zone to reach the final.With East set a target of 159 runs, the 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (40) and Ishan Kishan (39 n.o.) helped their team to reach the target with a day to spare on Tuesday. It was for the second straight match that East, who beat Northeast in the quarterfinal, wrapped up the match inside three days.All eyes were again on Vaibhav during the chase. Interestingly, there was a slight change in Vaibhav's approach. The Bihar boy, who hit only one six in his first 37 balls, cut loose in the 14th over to smash Yash Thakur for three fours and a six before his dismissal. Another attempted six off Thakur ended his innings with Central skipper Rajat Patidar taking a fine running catch.Though slow left-arm Harsh Dubey claimed four wickets -- Abhimanyu Easwaran, Virat Singh, Kumar Kushagra, Anukul Roy -- quickly, Ishan saw East home.Earlier, Central, who started the day on 45/3, lost wickets at regular intervals. Mukesh Kumar finished with a four-wicket haul while Mohammed Shami claimed three as Central lost their last seven wickets in the morning session.In the other semifinal, North Zone batters showed positive intent at the adjacent ground after South stretched their lead to 117. North, who were sitting pretty at 175/2, were reduced to 256/7 at stumps as they took their lead to 139 runs at the end of the penultimate day's play.The Delhi duo of Sanat Sangwan (76) and Ayush Doseja (52) kept the scoreboard ticking. However, pacer Vidwath Kaverappa, who did not take the field in the third session due to a leg injury, dismissed Doseja. New man Ayush Badoni then kept the momentum going with a brisk 37-ball 31, but North lost the plot after tea.In a span of 10 overs, South took five wickets before Nishant Sindhu (20 batting) and Anshul Kamboj (29 batting) stitched an unbeaten 47-run eighth-wicket stand to keep their side afloat. Earlier, South added 27 runs to their overnight total of 285/9 before being all out. Tilak Verma remained unbeaten on 116.
Article Summary: East Zone beat Central Zone by four wickets to reach Duleep Trophy final. 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Ishan Kishan helped East reach target with a day to spare. North Zone were reduced to 256/7 at stumps on penultimate day of semifinal.

Article Title: Cricket side under fire after signing player acquitted of rape, indecent assault charges

Cricket accessories (AFP Photo)

Kuggeleijn’s controversial past

Hampshire fighting to avoid relegation

Hampshire have faced a strong reaction from their own supporters after including controversial New Zealand cricketer Scott Kuggeleijn in their squad for the County Championship match against Warwickshire, despite not publicly announcing his signing.The 34-year-old was listed among Hampshire’s 15 players on X, with the county yet to officially confirm his arrival as an overseas player.Fans quickly criticised the move, with one calling it “a disgrace” and another describing it as “shameful” and “a new low for the club”.Kuggeleijn was charged in 2015 with sexual violation by rape and indecent assault involving two separate complainants. He was acquitted after a second trial, following a hung jury in the first trial.Despite the acquittal, his selection for New Zealand and domestic teams has repeatedly led to protests. In 2019, spectators at Eden Park held up posters objecting to his inclusion.Kuggeleijn has spent the past 12 years playing for Northern Districts in New Zealand and will now join Hampshire for the final four matches of their County Championship campaign.Hampshire are currently bottom of Division One and are 16 points behind Leicestershire, whom they still have to face.With the team battling to stay in the top division, Kuggeleijn’s arrival has added controversy away from the field.His inclusion has already sparked criticism from supporters, particularly because the club did not announce his signing before naming him in the squad.

Article Title: Pakistan cricket chaos: PCB seeks answers over Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq picks as Misbah-ul-Haq quits selection committee
Article Text:
Mohammad Rizwan and Imam-ul-Haq

PCB questions selection process

Misbah set to step down amid overhaul

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has sought an explanation from its national selection committee over the inclusion of Mohammad Rizwan and Imam-ul-Haq in the Test squad for the ongoing England series, adding another layer to the turmoil surrounding the side.According to a report by Geo News, the PCB issued a notice to members of the selection committee on August 31, asking them to explain the basis and rationale behind recommending Rizwan and Imam for the Test squad.The notice, a copy of which was seen by Geo News, directed committee members including Aqib Javed, Misbah-ul-Haq and Asad Shafiq to submit written explanations detailing the players’ performances, selection criteria and other factors considered during the process. The members have been given 24 hours from receipt of the notice to respond.The notice reportedly referred specifically to a selection committee meeting held on June 2, 2026. The minutes of that meeting were submitted on July 1, with members tasked with considering players for Pakistan’s Test squads for the tours of the West Indies and England.Rizwan and Imam were subsequently shortlisted on the committee members’ recommendations.The PCB’s move comes after Pakistan endured a disastrous start to the three-match Test series against England. They suffered an innings-and-103-run defeat in the opening Test before going down by 194 runs at Lord’s, handing England an unassailable 2-0 lead.Both Rizwan and Imam were subsequently released from the Test squad ahead of the third match at Edgbaston, beginning September 9.The PCB’s demand for an explanation comes amid a sweeping overhaul of the Pakistan Test setup.A day before the notice emerged, the board announced that seven players had been released from the squad. Alongside Rizwan and Imam, Salman Ali Agha, Ali Usman, Aamir Jamal, Muhammad Awais Zafar and Khurram Shahzad were also sent out.Pakistan have brought in seven replacements, including Test-capped batters Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal, while Arafat Minhas, Mohammad Imran Jnr, Saad Baig, Mohammad Imran and Razaullah have also been added.The coaching staff has undergone a major change as well, with head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul removed from their positions. White-ball head coach Mike Hesson and bowling coach Ashley Noffke have been brought in to oversee the side for the remainder of the England tour.The developments have also triggered uncertainty within the selection committee itself. Sources close to Misbah-ul-Haq said he has decided to resign from the committee , informing the PCB of his decision and agreeing to serve a notice period before formally stepping down.The former Pakistan captain’s reported decision adds another twist to an already chaotic period for Pakistan cricket, with the board now seeking answers from the very selection process that produced a squad it has subsequently overhauled midway through the England series.
Article Summary: Pakistan Cricket Board seeks explanation from national selection committee over inclusion of Mohammad Rizwan and Imam-ul-Haq in Test squad for England series. PCB issued a notice to members of the selection committee on August 31, asking them to explain the basis and rationale behind recommending the pair. The members have been given 24 hours from receipt of the notice to respond.

Article Title: Lhuan-dre Pretorius stars as South Africa beat Zimbabwe again to strengthen tri-series campaign
Article Text:
Lhuan-dre Pretorius

Pretorius powers South Africa to 185

Jansen, Fortuin dismantle Zimbabwe chase

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

South Africa continued their strong run in the Namibia T20I Tri-Series with another convincing victory over Zimbabwe, securing a comfortable 43-run win in the fourth match at the Namibia Cricket Ground on Tuesday.Lhuan-dre Pretorius narrowly missed out on a maiden T20I century but produced a career-best 94 to set up South Africa’s second victory over Zimbabwe in the tournament. The opener’s sensational knock came off just 51 balls and featured 12 fours and three sixes.Pretorius was named Player of the Match after helping South Africa post 185/7 before their bowlers completed the job by dismissing Zimbabwe for 142 in 17.4 overs.Put into bat, South Africa made an aggressive start, with Pretorius anchoring the innings and playing a key role in two partnerships of more than 50 runs for the first two wickets.He found an able partner in Dewald Brevis, who struck 41 off 27 balls, as the Proteas built a strong platform. Zimbabwe did manage to fight back with regular wickets towards the latter stages, but South Africa had already done enough damage to reach a competitive 185/7.Pretorius fell six runs short of a century, but the opener insisted the team victory mattered more than his individual milestone.“Yeah, that's fine. I'm just glad we got over the line. Milestones will come and go, and yeah, it wasn't meant to be today, but I was just glad because we said at the 14-over mark we wanted to get to 200, and I knew if I got the team to 200 I'd get to the milestone. But yeah, I think milestones come and go, and today was not meant to be, but we won, so it's good,” Pretorius said.Zimbabwe needed 186 for victory but struggled to maintain momentum after a promising beginning from Brian Bennett.Their powerplay was derailed by a double-wicket maiden from captain Bjorn Fortuin , and South Africa struck again soon after the fielding restrictions ended.Duan Jansen produced a decisive burst, taking three wickets in four balls across two overs to leave Zimbabwe in serious trouble.Captain Sikandar Raza offered some resistance with 45 off 33 balls, while Newman Nyamhuri added 27 with some aggressive hitting. But the pair could only reduce the eventual margin of defeat as Zimbabwe were bowled out for 142.Fortuin was the standout bowler, finishing with 4/24 from 3.4 overs, while Jansen claimed 3/21. The pair shared seven wickets between them as South Africa repeatedly struck at crucial moments.The result gives South Africa their second win over Zimbabwe in the tri-series, with Pretorius’ near-century and a disciplined bowling performance combining to secure another comprehensive victory.
Article Summary: South Africa beat Zimbabwe by 43 runs in the Namibia T20I Tri-Series. Lhuan-dre Pretorius scored a career-best 94 to help South Africa to 185/7. The Proteas bowled out Zimbabwe for 142 in 17.4 overs.

Article Title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi shines as East Zone beat defending champions Central Zone to reach Duleep Trophy final
Article Text:
East Zone's Vaibhav Sooryavanshi plays a shot on day three of the Duleep Trophy semi-final. (PTI Photo)

Sooryavanshi provides early spark before dramatic dismissal

Shami, Mukesh dismantle Central before Kishan finishes chase

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s aggressive cameo, backed by fiery spells from Mohammed Shami and Mukesh Kumar , helped East Zone storm into the Duleep Trophy final with a four-wicket win over defending champions Central Zone on Tuesday.The 15-year-old Sooryavanshi made a valuable contribution of 40 off 43 balls as East Zone chased down a target of 159 on a turning pitch on the third day of the semifinal.East, winners of the tournament in the 2012-13 season, will face either South Zone or North Zone in the final at Chepauk from September 6.Chasing 159, East needed a steady start as the pitch increasingly aided the spinners. Sooryavanshi initially adopted a cautious approach, scoring his first 15 runs from 30 balls.But once he found his rhythm, the left-hander shifted gears spectacularly. His next 25 runs came from just 13 deliveries, featuring another six and three boundaries.His opening partner Abhimanyu Easwaran was more fluent initially, including a six off off-spinner Saransh Jain over long-on, while Sooryavanshi struggled to find the same freedom against spin.The teenager, however, came alive when Yash Thakur was introduced into the attack.Having already hammered the pacer for four fours and two sixes in the first innings, Sooryavanshi again went after him, smashing three fours and a six in the 14th over.But his attacking approach also brought about his downfall. Sooryavanshi fell in the same over when Rajat Patidar completed a stunning running catch off Thakur.His dismissal suddenly changed the mood of the chase, with East losing wickets at regular intervals. Harsh Dubey then struck twice in successive deliveries, removing Kumar Kushagra and Anukul Roy to leave East at 124 for five.Earlier, Central resumed their second innings at 45 for three but suffered a dramatic collapse in the extended first session. They lost their remaining seven wickets to be bowled out for 158.Shami and Mukesh were the chief destroyers, exploiting variable bounce and the assistance available to the bowlers. Shami finished with 3/56, while Mukesh claimed 4/44 to complete a seven-wicket haul in the match.Mukesh was subsequently named Player of the Match, providing a timely boost to the India seamer who has been out of favour.Central briefly threatened to stretch the chase when Dubey and Arshad Khan added 43 for the ninth wicket, taking their side beyond 150. But East held their nerve to complete the victory.Ishan Kishan then produced a composed 39 not out from 41 balls to guide East home with minimal further trouble.“For a personal point of view, and not only me, the entire team members are looking forward to playing in the final. It will be heartening if we can go on and win that title,” Easwaran said after the match.

Article Title: Asian Games cricket row: Japan Cricket CEO says teams can make own arrangements

Korogi Sports Park built from scratch

NEW DELHI: With concerns over accommodation and other logistical arrangements emerging ahead of cricket’s return to the Asian Games , Japan Cricket Association (JCA) CEO Naoki Alex Miyaji has sought to put the apprehensions into perspective, saying participating teams have been offered hotel accommodation but are free to make their own arrangements.At a recent Asian Cricket Council (ACC) meeting, leading cricketing nations reportedly raised concerns over the accommodation arrangements, with the designated hotel located around 20km from the Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin City, Aichi Prefecture, where the cricket matches will be held.The Asian Games begin on September 17.Miyaji stressed that the JCA is playing a limited role in the event’s organisation.“The Asian Games is being organised by the organising committee Aichi-Nagoya Games Organizing Committee (AINAGOC) in collaboration with the ACC under the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA),” Miyaji told PTI.“The JCA has provided support in some areas but is not directly involved so I am not able to directly answer all of your questions. What I can say is that all parties are working hard to ensure the success of Cricket in the Asian Games.“I can also assure you that the ACC have been discussing accommodation options with AINAGOC for a long time. The participating teams in cricket are being offered hotel accommodation,” he said.Miyaji also pointed out that cricket is not the only sport facing logistical constraints at the Games.“Many other sports are being accommodated in much more limited facilities such as a cruise ship or container hotels. The teams are free to arrange their own accommodation if they chose to do so,” he said.Miyaji also sought to allay concerns over reports that team washrooms could be located at least half a kilometre from the playing arena.“Please note that toilets will be available within the player area. There are both temporary and permanent facilities at the venue. The facilities on the ground are temporary, but AINAGOC have worked very closely with the ACC for over a year now to ensure that the best facilities are provided within the limited timeline and facility restrictions,” Miyaji said.He also addressed concerns over the makeshift dressing rooms being prepared for the tournament.“Despite being temporary, the facilities will provide as comfortable a space as possible for the players and officials. There are also permanent facilities around the ground which will be available to the players,” he said.Miyaji explained that organisers had only 17 months to prepare the venue, which had to be developed from scratch because Aichi Prefecture did not have an established cricket facility.“They only had 17 months to prepare and had to start from scratch as there were no Cricket venues of any standard in Aichi Prefecture. Considering the limited time and resources available, AINAGOC and ACC have worked together to ensure that the playing facilities are suitable,” he said.Sri Lanka Cricket has also provided curators to work on the turf and hybrid pitches.“It will be a full size ground with turf and hybrid pitches prepared by the best curators which Sri Lanka Cricket should be credited for providing,” Miyaji said.“There are limits on what they can do within these tight limits, but from what I have seen, the playing surface and field will be the best seen in Cricket's inclusion in the Asian Games.”The JCA, meanwhile, has concentrated largely on building local interest in the sport.“We have taken cricket to many school and shopping centres which have received great enthusiasm. Thanks to the full support of Nisshin City, we are confident that the local community will be 100% behind the Asian Games.”Miyaji remained confident that cricket would make a strong impression when the continental event is staged in Japan.“Cricket will be one of the largest sports in the Asian Games. It will also be the first time the top Cricket teams of Asia will be playing in Japan,” he added.
Article Summary: Japan Cricket CEO clarifies accommodation arrangements. ‘Toilets will be available within the player area’ says Naoki Alex Miyaji. Korogi Sports Park built from scratch because Aichi Prefecture did not have an established cricket facility.

Article Title: Rajasthan stuck in 2012, Manipur in 2023: How actively are states with CWG medals promoting sports?
Article Text:
Are sports bodies of Indian states promoting the game properly?

Medal tally of India's athletes by birth state/UT

Haryana: Hit on the podium, not so much off it

Manipur still talking about 2023

Rajasthan: 14 years and counting

Uttar Pradesh and Delhi carry the same gloomy picture

And then come Tamil Nadu and others

The ones somewhere in the middle

How active are states/UTs with CWG medallists in promoting sport

Does it matter so much?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is more important for grassroots sports promotion? Social media presence Local sports events Government funding 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Somewhere on a muddy school field in Haryana right now, a teenager is perhaps drilling the same throwing technique over and over, just as she had watched on television just days ago. Her sole aim is to pull off the one like Sharmila Dhankar, India's Commonwealth Games shot put gold medallist.Before the 2026 CWG campaign, she, like many of us, had almost certainly never heard the name. And it's not because Dhankar had not won anything before the Glasgow Games; she had, a gold medal in the Women's Shot Put F57 event at the 2026 Fazza International Para Athletics Championship, but because one of the primary institutions whose entire job was to carry that story back from the medal podium to villages and training grounds across the state has, for all practical purposes, gone quiet.That's the part of this story that rarely gets told. India walked away from Glasgow with 39 medals, and for a week, the athletes who won them were everywhere, garlanded at airports, seated beside ministers, their faces on the evening news. But medals don't build the next generation of athletes by themselves. Somebody has to keep telling their stories, long after the felicitation photo is filed away, to the kid training in a dusty school ground who needs proof that this path actually leads somewhere.We wanted to know which state sports departments are still doing their job of promoting the sports and their grassroots on their social media platforms, and which ones seem to have simply logged off. So we scrolled through the timelines ourselves. Here's what we found.No state produced more glory in Glasgow than Haryana. Eleven medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze, spanning boxing, wrestling, athletics, and para sport, headlined by a Neeraj Chopra silver that will be replayed on sports channels for years.Alongside him were names most of India still had little knowledge of. The likes of Preeti Pawar, Jaismine Lamboria, Sakshi Chaudhary, Priya Ghanghas, Sachin Siwach, and Ankush Panghal, all of whom trained in government facilities, under government schemes, and who'd probably appreciate their own state department cheering as loudly for them as it does for its concert lineups.Because that's the thing. The Sports Department, Government of Haryana's X account has posted exactly once in all of 2026, and it's a flyer for the music acts playing at the Chief Minister's Cup.Facebook and Instagram follow a similar rhythm with a short cluster of posts around that February event, and then not much else.Eleven medals, and not one dedicated post to show for it. Somewhere in Rohtak or Bhiwani, a young pugilist training in Priya Ghanghas's discipline would probably just like a little proof that someone up top is paying attention.Manipur's page has an odd time-capsule quality to it. This is the state that gave India Mirabai Chanu, one of the country's most beloved Olympic medalists, and this Commonwealth Games alone produced four medalists from Manipur, Chanu's gold among them, alongside Rishikanta Singh, Bindyarani Devi, and Jadumani Singh.And yet the Department of Youth Affairs & Sports' X account hasn't posted since October 2023, a "Run for Unity" event, frozen well before any of this year's medals happened.Although the Facebook page has had a few sporadic posts here and there this year, its Instagram account has managed just two posts since January. It’s the kind of gap that makes you wonder if someone simply forgot the login details somewhere along the way.If there's one number in this whole exercise worth sitting with, it's this: the official Sports Department, Government of Rajasthan hasn't posted on Facebook since April 14, 2012.Fourteen years, through Arundhati Choudhary's Commonwealth gold and everything else that's happened in Rajasthan sport since.Its X account's last original post predates a retweet from March 2021, and there's no Instagram at all. A parallel handle, the Rajasthan State Sports Council, exists across all three platforms and is barely livelier.Somewhere behind Choudhary's medal is a genuinely good story, but it just hasn't found a home on the one page built to tell it.Gulveer Singh managed both a silver and a bronze for Uttar Pradesh this Games, a rare double that would make a great centrepiece for the state's sporting year. Instead, across two separate official handles on three platforms, Uttar Pradesh Sports has produced little beyond reposts, while its sister account, Sports Directorate, Govt of Uttar Pradesh, hasn't posted at all in 2026.Delhi Government, for its part, doesn't run a dedicated sports account at all on any of the popular social media platforms, so gold medalist Harsh Singh and bronze medalist Tejaswin Shankar, both representing India's capital, don't really have an institutional cheerleader online, their wins quietly absorbed into the general churn of city government updates. Both athletes are, in effect, doing their own promotional legwork.Set against all that quiet, Tamil Nadu feels like a different sport altogether. Its Sports Tamil Nadu handles post multiple times a day, celebrating not just its own three medalists, Praveen Chithravel, Selva Prabhu, Muthupandi Raja, but athletes from other states too, weaving in government scheme updates without it ever reading like bureaucracy.Every medallist got a dedicated post. Somewhere in Tamil Nadu, a kid training in long jump or wrestling doesn't have to wonder whether the sport leads anywhere. The state tells them, publicly, almost daily.Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka's Facebook and Instagram pages, Assam, Bihar, and Tripura all follow a version of that same habit, active, consistent, generous with attention toward athletes nobody outside their district would otherwise know existed.Kerala doesn't run a separate sports handle on X but keeps its Facebook and Instagram genuinely lively, making sure Murali Sreeshankar and Mohammed Basil's silvers got their due.Andhra Pradesh mirrors that same rhythm across all three platforms.Not every state falls neatly into being inactive or staying proactive. Punjab's account managed just two posts on X all year, New Year's and Republic Day, though its Facebook and Instagram carry a bit more life around coaching and departmental meetings, even if athletes rarely get top billing.Uttarakhand was genuinely active last year before cooling off in 2026, leaning more toward government scheme announcements on Facebook, though its Instagram at least carried two posts around the Games.Maharashtra has dedicated posts up for both Sarvesh Kushare and Dilip Gavit, with Instagram staying fairly regular, enough effort to stay out of the quiet column.Karnataka's X account hasn't posted since March 2024, around an unrelated cultural-team event, even though its Facebook and Instagram have stayed warm and active toward its CWG medalists.It is worth asking why this actually matters, beyond good manners. Well, a state sports department's social media feed isn't just a courtesy board for congratulations; it's one of the cheapest, most direct tools available to build the next generation of athletes.A youngster in a small town is far more likely to pick up a javelin because they saw a state government post celebrating someone from their own district. Even when it comes to promoting any government policy, social media can be as effective.Visibility drives aspiration. There's a funding logic too. Sponsors, corporates, and even state finance departments allocate resources partly based on visible public interest, and a well-run social account is often the easiest evidence a sport has that interest.ALSO READ: Anahat Singh: What is in the name? A word from Guru Nanak's prayer, now India's squash sensation Silence, on the other hand, sends the message that grassroots sport isn't a priority worth the effort of a single post, even when the state has just produced a medallist on the world stage.It is worth it because sometimes, the first step towards building a sporting culture is simply showing people that their achievements are being seen.
Article Summary: India won 39 medals at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Haryana produced 11 medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze. But the state sports department has posted just once in all of 2026. What do you think is more important for grassroots sports promotion? Government funding or social media presence? Share your view.

Article Title: ‘That video was not ordinary’: PM Modi praises Lovlina for objecting to distorted India map - Watch
Article Text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi shares a light moment with boxer Lovlina Borgohain. (PTI Photo)

‘That video was not ordinary’

Mirabai opens up about four difficult years

Narender's joke leaves Modi laughing
